MuleSoft's Customer Support team is looking for talented individuals with a passion for researching complex technologies and a track record of high customer satisfaction to help our team drive customer success with MuleSoft products. We maintain an extremely high level of satisfaction across our customer base, and we take great pride in our operational efficiency and the strength of the solutions we provide to our customers.

As a member of the Support team, you will leverage advanced technical expertise to resolve complex platform-related issues affecting customers. As a Senior Technical Support Engineer expert, you will enable customer success by helping our customers to overcome crippling technical challenges. You will provide hands-on troubleshooting, feature explanation, and best practice guidance to the broader Technical Support team to assist customers during critical and time-sensitive situations while partnering with development teams.

You'll find yourself researching new technologies every day, including Web Services, HTTP, JMS, JEE application servers, and many types of Enterprise Software. This role will give you an opportunity to build expertise and fast-track your career toward customer-facing technical roles, and your successes will have an impact across the company.

Work Hours: The candidate primarily needs to work US East or US Central shift. However, we are a 24x7 Support Hub, the candidate hence needs to be ready to work any shift based on business requirements.

Note: this role is office-flexible, and the expectation is to be in-office a minimum of three (3) days per week.


Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Take ownership of customer issues through to resolution - including troubleshooting, internal communication, and providing meaningful feedback on a regular basis to assist with troubleshooting integrations involving third-party APIs and implementation of other products.
  • Liaise and work closely with the internal teams on escalated technical issues and product roadmap changes/new features.
  • Provide feature explanation and implementation best practices.
  • Create knowledge base materials dedicated to operational efficiency while empowering and enabling the developer community.
  • Respond promptly and effectively to technical support requests from clients regarding integration API-related issues.
  • Diagnose and troubleshoot technical issues, offering timely and accurate solutions to ensure minimal disruption to clients' operations.
  • Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, including developers and operations, to resolve complex integration challenges.
  • Document and track support cases, solutions, and interactions in our support systems to maintain accurate records.
  • Escalate critical issues to development teams when necessary, ensuring timely resolution.



Minimum Requirements

  • Must be a US citizen on US soil and not a citizen of another country (dual citizen).
  • Must be able to obtain authorization to work on US government support cases
  • Bachelor's Degree or equivalent relevant experience required. Experience will be evaluated based on the core competencies for the role (e.g. extracurricular leadership roles, military experience, volunteer roles, work experience, etc.).
  • Strong understanding of REST and SOAP web-based services, with a working knowledge of WSDL interpretation, generation, and consumption.
  • Experience troubleshooting Internet technologies: HTTP, firewalls, web servers, proxy servers, etc.
  • In-depth knowledge of database concepts and data management (RDBMS) and SQL.
  • Proven analysis, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills. Ability to effectively prioritize and escalate customer issues.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.



Preferred Qualifications

  • MuleSoft Certifications (MCD 1, MCD 2) are a plus
  • Knowledge and troubleshooting experience with at least one programming language, such as Java, .NET, or PHP, and analyzing thread dumps and heap dumps as an added advantage.

  • Must have experience in Java development and concepts, including debugging against Java APIs, providing technical solutions, examining thread dumps and threading issues, and hosting services using JEE and/or JSE framework
  • Experience with JEE Application Servers and Containers (administration, deployment, and/or development in Tomcat, JBoss, WebSphere, Spring, etc.)

The Experience
Technical Program Managers (TPMs) lead large, cross-functional initiatives at Salesforce from start to finish, working closely with executives and key partners on the company’s most critical programs.

The Director of TPM for Missionforce will report to the SVP of Missionforce National Security and run a portfolio of high-stakes programs at the center of Salesforce’s national security business. The programs include M&A integration, large federal mission implementations (such as replacing an agency’s enterprise IT service management platform) and new commercial models such as outcome-based contracting and pricing.


The ideal candidate is as comfortable building a program V2MOM and running a steering committee as getting into the details of GovCloud onboarding or a contract structure. This individual contributor role is for someone who brings structure to ambiguity and moves fast with a sense of mission.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Help build the business case and investment requirements for future fiscal years.

  • 10+ years of program management, technical program management, consulting or engineering management experience, with at least some time at an enterprise technology company.

  • Experience delivering complex enterprise SaaS implementations or platform programs.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with hands-on attention to detail.
  • Strong executive communication and facilitation skills, and the ability to build consensus in a matrixed environment.
  • The ability to master new technical, commercial and contractual subjects quickly.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen (U.S. born or naturalized) living on U.S. soil who does not hold dual citizenship with the ability to meet customer and government screening standards applicable to this role. ​

  • Identify underutilized platform capabilities and incorporate them into migration roadmaps to increase customer throughput and adoption.

  • Serve as a subject matter expert in at least one key domain: Marketing Cloud (Engagement/Intelligence), Data 360 (Data Cloud), Revenue Cloud (CPQ/Billing), or Tableau.
  • Apply AI literacy and prompt engineering skills to guide AI agents in data retrieval, migration health reporting, and task automation.
  • Act as the technical point of contact during major migration incidents — coordinating with Engineering and Product to protect the customer's operations during cutover phases.
  • Monitor technical trends proactively and provide tailored release recommendations to optimize migrated environments for performance and stability.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in Professional Services, Customer Success, or Technical Consulting, with a strong focus on large-scale platform migrations.
  • Deep, hands-on domain expertise in one or more of the following: Marketing Cloud (Engagement/Intelligence), Data 360 (Data Cloud), Revenue Cloud (CPQ/Billing), or Tableau.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive business value, facilitate technical discussions, and navigate complex stakeholder conversations.
  • Ability to translate complex technical architectures into business-friendly language and guide customers through data transformations.
  • Proven experience working with global or offshore delivery models (such as GDC) to accelerate project delivery.
  • Advanced knowledge of Salesforce core (Sales/Service Cloud) or specialized clouds (Marketing, Data, Revenue, or Tableau).
  • Familiarity with AI agents or automation tools applied to data mapping, sentiment analysis, or task automation.
  • Understanding of how target cloud platforms integrate with telephony systems, third-party data sources, and self-service portals.
  • Degree or equivalent relevant experience required. Experience will be evaluated based on the core competencies for the role (e.g. extracurricular leadership roles, military experience, volunteer roles, work experience, etc.)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Certifications in relevant domains (e.g., Marketing Cloud Consultant, CPQ Specialist, Data Cloud Consultant, Tableau Desktop Specialist).
  • Prior experience as an individual contributor leading multi-million dollar transformation engagements.
  • Salesforce AI Associate or Agentblazer certifications.

You'll join a team that is shaping how Salesforce customers adopt the next generation of cloud technology — with access to cutting-edge AI tools, a collaborative global delivery model, and a direct line to the Product teams building the platforms you work with. The Senior Technical Consultant – Core (Sales & Service Cloud) is a hands-on execution role within the Strategic Migration CoE / Migration Factory. The role supports end-to-end migrations and implementations from legacy CRM platforms (e.g., Siebel, Microsoft Dynamics, legacy or custom CRMs, other Salesforce orgs) to Salesforce Sales Cloud and Service Cloud. Unlike the Technical Architect (who owns solution strategy and design), this role focuses on detailed technical implementation: platform configuration, declarative and programmatic development, data migration, integrations, and quality validation. You will work under the architect's guidance and in direct contact with client teams, and you will mentor junior consultants and set technical quality standards on the team.

PREFERRED

  • Enterprise Security is hiring a Director, Business Information Security Officer (BISO), also called a Security Partner. You are accountable for the security posture of major Enterprise Business Units (BUs) and serve as their primary link to the broader Security organization.
  • This is a senior technical leadership role. You read designs, understand the systems, and take clear positions on architecture, controls, and trade-offs with engineers, product leaders, and executives.

  • This role is based in NYC, NY; SF, CA; Denver, CO; Indianapolis, IN; Dallas, TX; or McLean, VA and is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement.



What You’ll Actually Be Doing

  • Own the security relationship for your assigned BU. Represent the customer’s voice inside Enterprise Security and security’s voice inside the customer’s leadership.
  • Own the risk register. Set severity, prioritization, and buy-down sequencing, accounting for compensating controls. Route risk-acceptance decisions to the right executive owner.
  • Build resourced risk buy-down plans with named owners and dates, hold teams accountable, and escalate when progress stalls.
  • Lead security input on design reviews, threat models, and architecture decisions. Shape the software development lifecycle (SDLC), secure-by-design patterns, and platform guardrails early.
  • Deliver quarterly reviews, risk narratives, and posture metrics ready for Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), Chief Information Officer (CIO), and Board audiences.
  • Bring in security engineers, the Cyber Security Operations Center (CSOC), technical program managers, and other specialists at the right time to drive outcomes the enterprise adopts.
  • Track emerging risks in AI and machine learning (ML) systems, such as agentic architectures, prompt injection, and model and training-data governance. Turn them into concrete risk and control decisions.
  • Consider compliance and regulatory requirements (such as FedRAMP, Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX), and regional data-protection laws) into your risk view to drive security prioritization, partnering with Legal, Privacy, and Compliance.
  • Drive adoption of security tooling, telemetry, and automation so risk decisions rest on data.
  • Manage, coach, and grow Security Partner Leads and Senior Leads. Set the operating cadence and the bar for deliverables, and develop successors.
  • Use approved AI assistants to produce executive-quality analysis and drafts, and help your team do the same.
  • Partner with Enterprise Security leadership on cross-portfolio strategy and enterprise-wide programs.



You’re Our Person If...

  • You have 12+ years of experience in cybersecurity engineering, IT risk, or a closely related field, including time in a large, complex enterprise.
  • You have served as a BISO, Security Partner, or similar senior security leader accountable for a business unit or product line.
  • You have managed and developed security professionals and built high-performing teams.
  • You have deep technical knowledge of cloud, identity, application security, and AI/ML risks, and can hold a substantive point of view in design reviews and threat models.
  • You know control frameworks such as COSO, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, and NIST SP 800-53, and regulations such as FedRAMP, SOX, and regional data protection.
  • You prioritize risk clearly and can explain what is the top risk and what is not worth fixing now, with rationale that holds up to executive scrutiny.
  • You have a record of measurably improving security in a business unit or product organization by closing findings, not just reporting them.
  • You communicate in writing and speaking at an executive level, including to CISO, CIO, and Board audiences.
  • You use sound judgment on when to decide, escalate, or hold the line, and you are comfortable challenging senior leaders.
  • You deliver in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and have experience with change events such as mergers and acquisitions (M&A), reorganizations, and product launches.

  • You build trust with senior technical and business leaders across distributed, cross-functional teams.

AEGIS is the availability engineering cloud that makes reliability a core feature of how Salesforce ships change. We use data, AI, and distributed systems to move the company from incident handled to incident prevented.

We are looking for a full-spectrum engineering leader to own a portfolio of services that are critical to Salesforce's availability posture. This is not just a service-delivery role. Join our Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) Security team in a fast-paced, strategic organization scaling through acquisition. This role is critical to successfully integrating new business acquisitions securely and efficiently.


You will act as the primary security partner for newly acquired companies, guiding them through our integration pipeline. Your core focus will be performing meticulous gap assessments and integration engineering to bring acquisitions to Salesforce's standards for security and inform integration priorities.


The ideal candidate is an innovative self-starter who balances deep technical security expertise with a collaborative, empathetic approach to partner integration.


Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Create comprehensive integration plans for security workstreams with risk-based integration priorities during the acquisition integration lifecycle.
  • Drive and close the security work required to bring acquired businesses under our organizational MSA, DPA, and SPARC frameworks.
  • Perform comprehensive infrastructure assessments on acquired environments.
  • Communicate clearly, empathetically, and effectively with newly acquired business partners to bridge security gaps collaboratively.
  • Prioritize critical security work in a highly dynamic, fast-paced M&A environment.
  • Execute robust threat models using the STRIDE methodology.
  • Independently drive your own work streams from start to finish without requiring heavy oversight.
  • Continuously innovate on our M&A security workflows, integration processes, and automation capabilities.

Minimum Requirements

  • Degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science or a relevant subject area, or equivalent experience.
  • Basic coding knowledge for application security (e.g., scripting, Bash, Terraform).
  • Deep understanding of the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability).
  • Demonstrated ability to prioritize complex security workflows and remediation efforts.
  • Proficiency in executing threat models using STRIDE.
  • Strong understanding of direct and transitive dependencies, as well as broader supply chain risks.
  • Ability to independently perform infrastructure assessments.
  • Well-versed in Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM).
  • Excellent communication skills, ability to tailor messaging for newly joining partners, requiring patience and leadership.
  • Versed in integrating and interpreting SAST (Static Application Security Testing) and DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) tooling.
  • Strong understanding of Zero Trust network architecture.
  • Expertise across Control, Data, and Application plane security.
  • Proficiency in secrets management best practices.
  • Deep knowledge of the path to production and build pipeline security (spanning source, build, artifact repository, and production deployment).
  • Experience with code and binary signing practices.
  • Experience with bug categorization and severity mapping.
  • Proficiency in data classification standards.
  • Clear understanding of what MSA, DPA, and SPARC frameworks entail for enterprise security.
  • Familiarity with SOC2 compliance requirements and controls.

  • Preferred Information security certifications (e.g., OSCP, OSEP, GPEN, GXPN, CISSP) or cloud security certifications.

Behind that growth is an equally important opportunity to transform how our own Public Sector teams operate. We are seeking a Service Management Analyst to help build the next generation of AI-powered engineering. Join our AI-native team as an early-career service manager to solve real production challenges, build intelligent automation and strengthen system reliability. With hands-on guidance from a senior mentor, you'll combine AI-assisted investigational skills with production support experience to grow into broader product or technical roles.


You'll investigate support cases, troubleshoot production issues and participate in support rotations—gaining firsthand insight into how complex systems work and where they can improve. Your mandate goes beyond resolving individual issues: you'll adopt and nurture AI-assisted solutions that eliminate recurring manual work and prevent problems from returning.


Your projects could include agentic case automation, trend analysis, automated access workflows, technical knowledge retrieval, log analysis and system hardening. You'll have the opportunities to own improvements from identifying the problem to measuring the result. It's a chance to learn through practical ownership, deliver meaningful improvements and build a foundation for a successful support & services career.


Must be a U.S. Citizen operating on U.S. Soil with ability to meet customer and government screening standards applicable to this role, including a Criminal Justice Information Services screening with fingerprint scan. Due to the citizenship requirement for this role, which supports U.S. federal, state, and/or local government customers, citizenship will be verified through two of the following REAL ID Act documents: U.S. Passport, Passport Card, REAL Driver's License, Global Entry Card, U.S. Government CAC/PIV.


What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Production Support & Monitoring
    • Monitor daily batch jobs, system health dashboards, and application alerts to catch and address anomalies before they impact end-users.
  • Incident & Problem Management
    • Participate in incident response and scheduled support or on-call rotations, with training and guidance appropriate to your experience.
    • Triage, troubleshoot, and document incoming production incidents (P1/P2 events), coordinate fix actions, and assist with root-cause analysis (RCA).
    • Partner with Engineering to improve code, monitoring, tests and documentation to prevent recurring incidents.
  • Application Lifecycle & Service Management
    • Track application performance metrics, maintenance windows, and compliance checks aligned with ITIL Service Operation frameworks.
    • Support to Salesforce Security mandates and best practices such as certification & token refresh, password rotation, QAR and federal audits.
  • Ticket & Request Handling
    • Manage service request fulfillment, user access coordination, and vendor-escalated support tickets within established SLAs.
    • Support Production Deployments
  • Tools & Automations
    • Build automation for recurring tasks such as access requests, case responses, log analysis, troubleshooting and maintenance.
    • Develop AI agents and workflows that help classify cases, retrieve relevant knowledge and execute approved actions with appropriate safeguards.
    • Help train AI agents to stay up-to-date, improve accuracy and efficiency.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
    • Act as an operational touchpoint between site IT, software engineering teams, and external third-party software vendors.
  • Reporting & Documentation
    • Compile operational KPI reports, update runbooks and knowledge-base articles, and document recurring system anomalies or process gaps.

  • A technical background, such as an MIS degree or a CS minor, with an understanding of computer systems and troubleshooting. Writing code is not required.
  • A Salesforce Platform Administrator I certification. The advanced certification can come after joining.
  • At least one internship or some industry experience
  • Willingness to work swing shifts and take PagerDuty on-call rotation
  • An ability to investigate problems using logs, error messages and system behavior.
  • Clear communication, a collaborative approach and a willingness to ask questions and learn from feedback.
  • Self-starter, willing to learn new technologies (Mulesoft, AI, Agentforce) and a Salesforce trailblazer who thrives on working in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to engage with self awareness as required to avoid conflicts with customers based on personality differences and to make suggestions in a manner that is more likely to result in a desired outcome.

Even Better If...

  • Experience with sandboxes and deployments, and familiarity with Salesforce enterprise environment, SOX protocols, Change Management and Release Management standards
  • Platform or Salesforce internship experience, familiarity with PagerDuty or incident management, and basic AI literacy
  • Curiosity and a passion for helping end users discover and resolve issues, asking good questions, breaking problems down and thinking on your feet
  • Initiative, such as self-study or certifying on your own, and comfort with operational, on-call work

The Service Management Analyst serves as an individual contributor within the operations and service management team. As a Senior Architect on the Customer Success Readiness & Comms team, you make sure Salesforce's infrastructure, platform, and security changes land smoothly for customers, partners, Support, and the field. You own the strategy, communications, and enablement across multiple concurrent infrastructure and product changes. You become the Subject Matter Expert, with a deep understanding of every behavior change, enforcement date, and extension path. You distill and share what you know internally and externally before customers feel the change.

You are the connective thread between Product Management, Engineering, Support, Security, and the field. You translate complex infrastructure, platform, and security changes into clear knowledge articles, playbooks, customer communications, and training. You also represent the customer and Support voice back into the product and program teams, so readiness gaps are found and closed early.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Assess readiness and prerequisites for critical product changes owned by the Identity and Developer Platform teams. Track status, dependencies, and risks in a project management tool.
  • Own the comms and enablement plan across a long-term project that includes multiple critical product changes. Set milestones, track delivery against enforcement dates, and escalate risks early.
  • Author, publish, and maintain customer-facing knowledge articles on help.Salesforce. Work with content writers and use the official publishing process.
  • Build and maintain internal Support knowledge articles, FAQs, and playbooks so Support is ready before enforcement dates.
  • Create and send comms and enablement assets: customer emails, internal Slack announcements, internal slides, and training. Follow a documented review and approval process for these assets.
  • Co-own the field-facing asset that is the primary internal resource on upcoming security-related product changes.
  • Lead the weekly Support swarm leads call with Support comms and enablement partners.
  • Present in an internal webinar series. Schedule, prepare, and support customer webinars (PMs usually present; you present and answer FAQs as needed).
  • Identify recurring themes from incoming questions, and feed them back into content and product feedback.
  • Define the comms and enablement approach for customer extension and self-service experiences. Cover when customers should use them, plus Support's role and edge cases.
  • Make day-to-day decisions on Comms & Enablement scope, content, and timing. Escalate cross-program issues to the manager and T&P Technology Program Managers.
  • Aggregate feedback and insights across Product, Engineering, Support, and the field to surface emerging risks and inform cross-functional decisions.
  • AI-First Delivery & Productivity Strategy: Drive the strategic scaling and champion the adoption of authorized AI technologies throughout your deliverables.



Minimum Requirements

  • 5+ years in a Customer Success, Product Management, Technical Program Management, Product Marketing/Enablement, or similar individual contributor role in the SaaS industry.
  • Hands-on understanding of the Salesforce platform.
  • Preferred, not required: working knowledge of identity and security concepts, such as OAuth flows (username-password, user-agent, device, refresh tokens), Connected Apps / External Client Apps, SSO, MFA, and SOAP login().
  • Experience driving release, readiness, or change-management motions for high-impact, customer-facing changes, ideally security or platform changes with enforcement dates.
  • Proven record of writing customer-facing and internal support content (knowledge articles, FAQs, playbooks, customer emails, release communications) that is accurate, clear, and usable by non-experts.
  • Experience enabling Support, Success, and field teams through training, webinars, and canvases or other enablement assets.
  • Experience working with technical and non-technical stakeholders across Product, Engineering, Support, Security, and GTM. Able to turn technical detail into clear, actionable guidance.
  • Demonstrated expertise in AI productivity tools, paired with a strategic, practical vision for leveraging them in forecasting, documentation, and tracking.



Skills & Expertise

  • Executive and Written Communication: Strong oral and written communication. Proven record of presenting to and updating internal and external stakeholders, including executives and customers.
  • Technical Translation: Can take complex infrastructure and product changes and make them understandable to Support, the field, and customers.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Can partner across Product Management and Engineering, Support, and Security teams to align priorities and drive coordinated execution.
  • Program Management and Execution: Can manage multiple concurrent workstreams, trackers, and deadlines. Keeps handoffs and approvals clean and holds stakeholders accountable.
  • Prioritization Agility: Shifts focus when enforcement dates, scope, or product readiness change. Manages through ambiguity (for example, processes still in development).
  • Critical and Strategic Thinking: Synthesizes input from many sources, spots themes and risks, and turns them into actionable plans.
  • Decision Quality: Makes sound decisions from analysis, experience, and judgment under competing priorities.
  • Conflict Management and Negotiating: Handles disagreements on scope, timing, and messaging with minimal noise. Wins buy-in without damaging relationships.

  • Data-Informed Decision Making: Uses quantitative and qualitative data (support case themes, channel questions, readiness status) to improve content and approach.

Help build the next generation of Agentforce. We’re an entrepreneurial incubation team within Salesforce, combining the pace and ownership of a startup with access to enterprise customers and Salesforce’s distribution. We’re looking for a technical product leader with deep AI expertise who wants to turn frontier capabilities into products customers can rely on.

Our team works closely with AI researchers, applied scientists, and engineers, uses coding agents extensively, and builds and experiments outside the core platform to iterate quickly. You’ll shape product strategy for AI quality and evaluation, establish how we measure progress, and personally lead a customer quality workstream and a focused feature from early learning through delivery.

This is a hands-on individual contributor leadership role, with an IC focus expected through 2027. You’ll lead through product ownership, technical judgment, and cross-functional influence while coaching colleagues, including junior designers and technical program managers. People-management responsibilities may develop as the product and team grow. You should enjoy inspecting traces and data, challenging evaluation results, prototyping with coding agents, and working directly with customers. Engineering partners own technical architecture and production implementation.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Set a coherent product strategy and roadmap for AI quality and evaluation, connecting customer needs, technical opportunities, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Establish shared quality definitions, evaluation requirements, coverage priorities, and release criteria with research, engineering, and product partners.
  • Make explicit investment tradeoffs across customer quality improvements, evaluation capabilities, and product features; align teams on priorities and decision ownership.
  • Personally lead customer investigations and experiments. For example, investigate why an agent gives an incorrect answer or fails a tool-driven workflow, define the expected behavior, and partner with researchers and engineers to test a change and validate its customer impact.
  • Build an operating approach that connects customer feedback, evaluation evidence, experiments, releases, and learning across teams.
  • Partner with researchers, applied scientists, and engineers to design credible evaluations. Apply AI/ML fundamentals such as training/test separation, overfitting, representative coverage, and independent validation to assess non-deterministic model behavior and grader reliability.
  • Lead delivery of capabilities that help customers understand and improve AI performance. For example, prototype an experience that turns a failed agent interaction into an evaluation case, makes the quality gap clear, and helps a customer verify whether a proposed change works.
  • Coach product partners, junior designers, and technical program managers in problem framing, experimentation, and delivery; raise the quality of decisions through mentorship and practical example.
  • Bring verified competitive insight into strategy and communicate differentiation, limitations, and investment choices clearly to customers and senior stakeholders.



Minimum Requirements

  • A record of building AI/ML products and delivering measurable customer outcomes, with increasing ownership, scope, and impact.
  • Deep hands-on experience building AI agents and evaluation capabilities in close partnership with AI researchers, applied scientists, or AI engineers. One to two years of substantive generative AI experience can be sufficient when supported by strong AI/ML fundamentals and demonstrated impact.
  • Strong applied AI/ML judgment across model behavior, prompting, retrieval, agent/tool workflows, and the tradeoffs among model, data, system, and product improvements.
  • Current hands-on ability to inspect data and traces, prototype with coding agents, and reason about experiments, overfitting, training/test splits, edge cases, and uncertainty. You can define what good looks like for a non-deterministic system and challenge conclusions with technical partners.
  • Principled, flexible thinking: frame the underlying customer problem, test assumptions, and change direction when evidence warrants it. You can explain when lessons from a previous product apply and when the context demands a different approach.
  • Experience establishing shared standards and resolving cross-team disagreements while preserving clear accountability and delivery momentum.
  • Evidence of coaching and mentoring colleagues without relying on reporting authority, and the ability to deliver independently in a fast-moving environment.
  • Clear communication with customers, technical teams, and senior leaders, including an honest account of what is known, uncertain, or still unproven.

  • Evaluation platforms, agent systems, AI observability, retrieval, or enterprise AI products.
  • Building in an AI-native startup or entrepreneurial environment, taking a new product from early customer learning to adoption, and applying lessons from both successful and unsuccessful experiments.
  • Hands-on prototyping with coding agents and delivery of customer-facing performance or outcome experiences.
  • Leading initiatives that require agreement across research, engineering, product, and customer-facing organizations.

Customers see credible improvement in real agent workflows, supported by evaluations they can trust. You independently take an initial quality problem from failure analysis through experimentation and customer validation, and deliver a focused feature with engineering. Teams make better release and investment decisions because of the evidence, product judgment, and coaching you bring.

About the Role

Production experience required. Builder mindset non-negotiable.
 

Salesforce is hiring Forward Deployed Engineers — experienced Technical Builders who design, build, and deploy agentic AI solutions directly inside enterprise customer environments. You'll work as part of a delivery team, partnering closely with a Deployment Strategist (Strategic Builder - a customer-facing advisor who shapes AI strategy and drives adoption) to co-build solutions that go live in production environments from day one. Engagements range from a single large strategic customer to multiple accounts simultaneously. The common thread is real code, real environments, and measurable business impact. This work spans configuration, customisation, and full-stack deployment — shipping solutions customers depend on.


The Builder Experience

  • AI-Powered Development: Ship real customer solutions, supported by best-in-class AI tools — Cursor, Claude, and Salesforce coding products like Vibes — embedded into your day-to-day workflow.
  • Collaborative Delivery: You'll work alongside Senior Forward Deployed Engineers and a Deployment Strategist. You'll own real components, benefit from structured mentorship from people who've shipped agentic systems at scale, and have a clear path to leading complex deliveries yourself.
  • Frontier Access: Our agentic AI platform is evolving in real time.  You'll work on capabilities most engineers won't touch for months — spanning Agentforce, data, platform, and headless architectures  and your field insight will feed directly to the product teams building them. 
  • Continuous Innovation: You'll be expected to stay at the forefront, experimenting with emerging AI tools, models, and frameworks, and sharing what you learn with your team and customers.


What You'll Actually Be Building

  • Develop AI agents and experiences that take real actions for real organisations. Our solutions are in production at some of the largest enterprises on the planet. The work matters because the customers depend on it.
  • Design agent intelligence: prompts, reasoning, tool calls, and integration with customer systems, leveraging our Agentic AI platform  and current LLM techniques.
  • Own technical components end-to-end: from architecture choice to deployed, validated, and observable in production.
  • Build and integrate data pipelines on Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake, Databricks, and customer data platforms. Model the data, ship the pipeline, validate the output
  • Build and maintain agent performance dashboards and customer KPI reporting to track deployment health and business outcomes.
  • Contribute to proofs-of-concept and MVPs that move from sketch to deployable in days, not months.
  • Co-build alongside customers and partners, sharing best practices and enablement as you go. Leaving teams more capable after each engagement than before.
  • Surface platform gaps, edge cases, and field insights to senior Engineers and the  product team. Your real-world experience is the product feedback loop.
  • Partner with the Deployment Strategist  in your pod to translate customer business challenges into agentic solutions that actually ship.


You're Our Forward Deployed Engineer If…

  • You have 3+ years of software engineering or technical delivery experience, with at least one production system you'd be proud to walk us through - ideally in an AI tech stack, full-stack development, or working with frontier models
  • You have a degree in Computer Science or a related field
  • You have prior customer-facing technical delivery experience (consulting, professional services, or forward deployed engineering) — this is a requirement, not a nice-to-have.
  • You're fluent in at least one of Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or Apex — and willing to add to that list as the work demands.
  • You've been hands-on with LLMs and prompt engineering. You can explain why a prompt failed and what you'd change.
  • You understand data modeling, APIs, and integration patterns deeply enough to design them, not just consume them.
  • You can hold your own in a room with sales teams and customer architects.
  • You ship quality code and evaluate AI outputs with engineering rigor.
  • You actively tinker with the evolving AI/data landscape — piloting new tools, experimenting with new models, and staying genuinely curious about what's coming next.
  • You thrive in the group chat that's building something, not just talking about it.
  • You're excited to travel ~25% of the time, working directly alongside customers.


Nice-to-Haves

  • Salesforce platform experience or certifications (Administrator, Platform Developer I, Agentforce Specialist)
  • Familiarity with agent frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) and orchestration patterns
  • Hands-on with cloud data platforms (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery)

You will help shape the global real estate footprint and strategy by planning the portfolio against workforce priorities, modeling buy versus lease, renewal, and exit decisions, and pressure-testing spend with our largest vendors. Deliver one consistent view of actuals, commitments, and outlook across COFO Finance.
  • Shape portfolio strategy: Partner with Real Estate Strategy to evaluate and model strategic transactions, including new leases, renewals, consolidations, exits, portfolio optimization, and buy vs. lease decisions. Frame the trade-offs, provide insights, and make a clear recommendation.

  • Drive vendor and spend insight: Lead full-relationship evaluations of our larges vendors, partnering with Procurement to identify savings and reinvestment opportunities.
  • Brief executives: Prepare COFO QBR materials and the quarterly CEO/ELT real estate review, translating complex results into clear recommendations and decisions.
  • Modernize with AI and automation: Build and deploy AI-enabled workflows, Business Intelligence, and planning tools that automate consolidation, variance commentary, and forecasting, and speed up reporting.
  • Partner across Finance: Bring financial expertise to cross-functional initiatives with Corporate FP&A, Technical Accounting, Procurement, and Finance leadership.
  • Lead and develop your team: Coach a high-performing team, building a culture of ownership, intellectual curiosity, and financial rigor.


Required Skills & Experience:

  • 10+ years in FP&A, corporate or strategic finance or commercial real estate company, including 2+ years leading people.
  • Advanced financial modeling, including scenario and “what-if” analysis for long-range plans and transaction economics.
  • Strong executive communication, written and verbal, with the ability to turn complex data into decision-ready recommendations.
  • Proven stakeholder influence: building trust, guiding teams through change, and driving financial accountability.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a quantitative field.

  • Experience in global corporate real estate, business operations at a large technology company, workplace, or facilities finance (leases, capital projects, workplace services).

  • Practical experience applying AI and automation to financial reporting, forecasting, or operational workflows.

You are both a big-picture automotive enterprise thinker and a deep, hands-on problem solver. You take pride in designing systems that withstand high transaction volumes across distributed dealer networks, support complex OEM-to-dealer data hierarchies, and will not fail at critical inflection points such as vehicle launch campaigns, service recall operations, or connected vehicle data ingestion spikes. The solutions you design are built for long-term scalability, growing seamlessly alongside the customer's dealer network footprint and connected vehicle ecosystem.
You have a strong mix of technical depth and enterprise consulting acumen, knowing how to leverage AI development tools like Claude, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot to optimize code quality, accelerate architectural design cycles, and rapidly prototype automotive-specific configurations. As Salesforce leads the agentic era, you play a front-line role in driving AI-First delivery—designing autonomous agents that power intelligent dealer assist, predictive service scheduling, and connected vehicle conversational experiences.

Stakeholder Collaboration: Collaborate with automotive client stakeholders—CTO, VP Digital, Head of Dealer Operations—to define requirements, deliverables, and manage expectations across enterprise OEM and dealer network engagements.
Solution Architecture: Translate complex automotive business requirements into well-architected Salesforce solutions, identifying opportunities to embed autonomous AI using Agentforce for intelligent dealer assist, predictive service agents, and connected vehicle conversational experiences.
Enterprise AI Architecture: Design and integrate scalable predictive and generative AI solutions within Automotive Cloud environments—optimizing performance, resource consumption, and platform governor limits to support real-time telematics ingestion and high-volume dealer operations.

Performance Evaluation & ROI: Collaborate with automotive customers to develop evaluation frameworks measuring AI performance, dealer satisfaction scores, service retention rates, and business value for specific automotive use cases.
Pre-Sales & Prototyping: Participate in automotive discovery workshops, technical deep-dives, and rapid POC development—using AI tools to prototype Vehicle Console configurations, dealer portal experiences, and Agentforce automotive agents for prospective clients.
Product Team Liaison: Liaise with Salesforce Automotive Cloud product teams to channel client implementation feedback, influence roadmap decisions, and ensure implementations align with platform evolution.

Based in Buenos Aires, you will support our customers across LATAM. Strong problem-solving skills are essential for navigating their challenges and finding innovative solutions.

title: LMTS - Lead AI/ML Engineer (LLM Post-Training)
descriptionHtml:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

What You'll Be Doing & Why It Matters

Salesforce has immediate opportunities for engineers who want their work to shape how trusted enterprise AI is trained, evaluated, and delivered. You will work with a group of world-class engineers to train and post-train open-weight language models for demanding enterprise workflows.

This is a model-training role, not a wrapper around a hosted LLM and not a prompt-engineering-only role. You will own the complete post-training loop: data generation, supervised fine-tuning, preference or reinforcement learning when appropriate, rigorous evaluation, and production serving. You will materially improve the behavior of models, not merely integrate model APIs.

The role encompasses ML research engineering, data generation, fine-tuning, evaluation, inference systems, and technical leadership. You will own code, experiments, evaluation evidence, and production behavior. We value demonstrated engineering judgment and reproducible results over credentials, paper claims, or an extensive keyword list.

We pride ourselves on building high-quality, maintainable systems that make the model more capable without compromising trust, safety, or operability. We embrace the hybrid model and celebrate the individual strengths of each team member while encouraging everyone to grow into the best version of themselves. We believe autonomous teams with the freedom to make decisions empower our people, products, company, and customers to thrive.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Train, adapt, and serve capable, reliable open-weight language models for enterprise workflows.
  • Own fine-tuning experiments from baseline through release: choose training objectives, run SFT and LoRA/QLoRA recipes, compare checkpoints against rigorous held-out evaluation, and diagnose failures before the next run.
  • Generate high-quality domain training data at scale, including synthetic instruction data, multi-turn conversations, reasoning and tool-use trajectories, structured outputs, counterexamples, preference pairs, and difficult evaluation cases.
  • Build the data engine behind post-training: source-grounded authoring, quality filtering, deduplication, contamination controls, dataset versioning, train/validation/test splits, packing, tokenization, and loss masking.
  • Design and run post-training experiments beyond SFT when justified, including DPO, ORPO, GRPO, RLVR, distillation, and other preference or reinforcement-learning methods. Match the method to a measured capability problem and a defensible reward signal.
  • Design and operate model-quality evaluation: held-out task suites, model-based and human review, tool-use and structured-output accuracy, multi-turn reliability, safety regressions, ablations, and error analysis.
  • Investigate model behavior deeply: identify whether a failure comes from data quality, training objective, model capacity, decoding, context handling, tool interface, or serving behavior, then produce evidence for the corrective action.
  • Build and ship high-quality, production-grade software using modern engineering practices, with AI as a core part of your development workflow.
  • Build reliable model-serving and inference capabilities, balancing quality, latency, throughput, memory use, and operational reliability.
  • Build robust integrations between models, tools, and enterprise systems, including structured outputs, function calling, and multi-step agent behavior.
  • Make architecture and design decisions with strong attention to model quality, reproducibility, performance, security, scalability, and future extensibility.
  • Improve observability, traceability, failure analysis, test coverage, and developer workflows across the training and serving lifecycle.
  • Work with domain experts to turn real workflows, product behavior, APIs, and failure cases into independently verifiable training and evaluation material.
  • Protect customer and company data: use approved sources only, preserve provenance, and keep credentials and sensitive data out of training and model prompts unless specifically authorized.
  • Review model, data, and application changes for factual correctness, quality, security, performance, and operational risk.
  • Mentor engineers and provide technical guidance that raises the quality bar across the team.

Minimum Requirements

  • 10+ years of software engineering experience, including technical leadership on production systems.
  • Strong Python engineering experience building and maintaining reliable production systems.
  • Hands-on ownership of LLM post-training. You have trained or materially improved open-weight language models through SFT and LoRA/QLoRA. Experience with preference optimization, RL, distillation, or continued pre-training is strongly valued. API integration alone does not qualify.
  • Hands-on ownership of training-data generation and curation. You have produced, filtered, reviewed, and versioned task-specific datasets, including synthetic instruction data, conversations, reasoning traces, tool calls, preference data, or structured outputs.
  • Strong practical understanding of the post-training stack: chat templates, tokenizer behavior, sequence packing, loss masking, optimizer and learning-rate schedules, checkpointing, distributed or memory-efficient training, and inference tradeoffs.
  • Experience creating and evaluating reasoning, tool-use, or structured-output training data. You understand the difference between a plausible trace and a correct, useful outcome, and know how low-quality traces degrade a model.
  • Experience with model evaluation: held-out datasets, error taxonomy, task and quality metrics, experiment design, ablation studies, regression analysis, and human-review workflows.
  • Strong software-engineering fundamentals: API design, testing, debugging, observability, version control, and clear technical writing.
  • Ability to investigate ambiguous failures across model behavior, data, prompts, retrieval, tools, and backend services.
  • Demonstrated leadership in architecture, design reviews, code reviews, and mentoring engineers.
  • Comfortable working across application and ML layers instead of staying within a narrow specialty.
  • A demonstrated, genuine AI-first approach to engineering — using AI to move faster, build fluency across the stack, and contribute well beyond your core specialty.
  • Experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cursor, etc.) in development workflows.
  • Advanced prompt engineering skills and the ability to write precise, structured prompts and cultivate the system context that makes AI outputs reliable, secure, and production-ready.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building integrations with enterprise platforms, APIs, data systems, identity controls, or tool-using AI applications.
  • Experience with complex enterprise workflows, such as CRM, commerce, finance, service, supply chain, or regulated-industry systems.
  • Deep experience with preference optimization or reinforcement-learning methods for LLMs, such as DPO, ORPO, GRPO, PPO, or verifiable-reward training. Candidates must be able to explain the reward/preference data, training stability, and failure modes, not just name a framework.
  • Resource-constrained or distributed model training and inference, including PyTorch, Transformers, TRL, Accelerate, DeepSpeed, FSDP, vLLM, GPU optimization, or quantized model serving.
  • Retrieval systems, source provenance, and retrieval evaluation. Retrieval experience is useful, but candidates must understand that retrieval is context, not a substitute for model training or model evaluation.
  • Security and data-governance work involving sensitive enterprise data, access scopes, auditability, and human approval boundaries.
  • Experience taking an AI feature from experiment through a measured, monitored production release.

What We Will Ask You To Show

  • Please be ready to discuss work you personally did. Strong candidates can explain:
  • One model-training project they owned end to end: base model, training objective, dataset scale and provenance, compute setup, training recipe, evaluation, production outcome, and what failed.
  • One dataset they generated for fine-tuning: source material, generation method, filtering and review, split strategy, known failure modes, and the evidence that it improved the model.
  • The actual training method they used, including why it was chosen over alternatives, how they tuned it, and how they knew it improved behavior rather than merely format-following.
  • One reasoning, tool-use, preference, or reinforcement-learning dataset they created or used: how correctness was established, how contamination was prevented, and how reward hacking or low-quality traces were detected.
  • The exact denominator, dataset split, and review method behind any quality or business-impact metric on their resume.
  • A difficult production incident or model-quality regression, how they isolated the cause, and the evidence that confirmed the fix.
  • A code sample, design document, experiment report, publication, or other artifact that makes their contribution verifiable. Confidential details may be redacted.
  • We do not require a PhD, publications, or prior domain experience. We do require depth, honesty about individual contribution, and the ability to turn claims into technical evidence.

We are looking for a technically strong Security Governance professional who can bridge the gap between Security & Compliance requirements and Engineering implementation. You sit with engineering, partner with GRC and auditors, and help service teams ship products that meet regulatory and customer trust requirements without drowning in audit work.

This role will serve as the technical voice and face of Compliance. You will partner closely with Engineering organizations, Product Security, Legal, and other stakeholders to understand how security and compliance requirements are implemented in real systems. You will identify what is working and what is not, and translate those insights back into practical, scalable governance requirements.

You will drive alignment of our services with frameworks such as SOC, ISO, PCI, HIPAA and public-sector requirements; lead compliance reviews in the SDLC; and run practical risk identification, treatment, and reporting so leaders can make risk-based decisions.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Review policy changes for compliance impact and translate them into clear engineering guidance
  • Support change management and CAB so changes stay compliant and do not introduce unnecessary risk
  • Own MuleSoft Compliance Controls and validate they are compliant with designated frameworks
  • Review, validate, and approve control attestations with control owners
  • Prepare teams for audit walkthroughs, keep interviews in scope, and streamline evidence collection (including automation where possible)
  • Drive remediation of audit findings: define done, timelines, risk, and validate the fix
  • Identify, prioritize, treat, and monitor trust risks (compliance, security, reliability) and report them to engineering leadership
  • Build automation and technical enforcement so compliance scales instead of becoming manual toil



You're Our Person If...

  • Experience in GRC, compliance engineering, security assurance, or a similar role inside a product or platform engineering org
  • Working knowledge of SOC 2, ISO 27001, and at least one of PCI, SOX, FedRAMP, or other regulated frameworks
  • Ability to read architecture and control implementations and explain them to both engineers, leaders, and auditors
  • Strong written and verbal communication; comfortable influencing without direct authority
  • Track record of audit prep, evidence review, and closing findings with engineering partners
  • Comfort with risk assessment: likelihood, impact, treatment, and a living risk register
  • Track the Direction of Compliance Frameworks - Monitor where regulatory and compliance expectations are heading, including AI governance, the EU AI Act, evolving international requirements, and market-specific regulatory expectations. Proactively identify implications for the organization.



Even Better If...

  • Experience with compliance automation, control-as-code, or evidence pipelines
  • Background in cloud / PaaS / SaaS multi-tenant architectures
  • Familiarity with change management, SDLC gates, or control attestation programs
  • Public-sector or Hyperforce / regional certification experience



Work authorization: U.S. citizenship required by federal regulation. Work must be performed on U.S. soil.

First 90 days: You understand the infrastructure and control inventory and own control remediation

6 Months: You begin to take ownership of the environment, assist remediation of any control gaps found, and drive compliance by design into engineering teams.

12 Months: You take ownership of MuleSoft compliance leading security and compliance assessments, keeping the team audit-ready, and strengthening governance across Mulesoft.

About Experience Strategy & Studio

Experience Strategy & Studio helps Salesforce decide where to go next—and makes that direction tangible. We bring customer insight, business ambition, and emerging technology together to identify opportunities that span products and organizational boundaries. Through focused, multidisciplinary missions, we build and test working experiences that clarify the opportunity, challenge assumptions, and guide product and investment decisions.

You’ll join a small, hands-on team working closely with Product, Engineering, Research, and Experience Architecture. The work moves from open questions to tangible proof, with successful ideas progressing into committed product plans and clear ownership for delivery.

We’re hiring a Principal Design Engineer. You’ll work at the intersection of design and engineering, turning consequential experience ideas into working, technically credible prototypes and reference experiences. Your work will help teams test what is possible, understand what is valuable, and decide what deserves further investment.

You’ll join focused, multidisciplinary missions with design, product, engineering, and research partners. You’ll bring technical depth and interaction craft to early concepts, expose implementation risks, and make ambitious possibilities tangible through code. You’ll use AI and agents in your practice and help teams find effective ways to build and learn. As promising work moves forward, you’ll help the receiving Product and Engineering teams understand the technical choices and carry the experience into production.

We value people who think deeply, communicate clearly, welcome critique, and improve the work through collaboration. Your impact will come through both what you build and the capabilities, judgment, and practices you help others develop.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Build working prototypes and reference experiences that answer a mission’s most important design and technical questions. Challenge the brief, explore new interaction possibilities, and make behavior, feasibility, and tradeoffs tangible enough for users and partners to evaluate.
  • Develop deep knowledge of the platforms, frameworks, and runtime environments relevant to your work. Balance established patterns with new approaches, making deliberate choices about accessibility, performance, maintainability, and experience quality.
  • Help designers and engineers work effectively with code and agents through practical examples, tools, documentation, and training. Establish ways to provide context, review generated work, and validate behavior before adoption.
  • Create the components, interactions, and prototyping approaches needed to test ambitious concepts with high craft. Work with design, engineering, and platform partners to use shared foundations where appropriate and surface gaps that the work reveals.
  • Partner with design, product, and engineering leaders to resolve difficult experience and implementation questions. Bring a clear point of view, invite challenge, and build commitment around shared decisions and priorities.
  • Use user feedback and technical evaluation to narrow, redirect, or stop approaches that are not proving valuable. Make implementation constraints and remaining uncertainties explicit, and support transfer to Product and Engineering owners with working code, design intent, and a credible path to production.



Minimum Requirements

  • 8+ years of experience at the intersection of product design and software engineering, with deep hands-on fluency in building interactive experiences in code.
  • Clarity and judgment: A record of turning uncertain concepts into working prototypes that expose the right questions, clarify tradeoffs, and influence what teams build.
  • Craft and technical depth: Exceptional interaction design judgment and engineering skill, including attention to motion, visual detail, feedback, accessibility, and performance. Show working examples where your engineering and design decisions substantially improved a delivered experience, and explain your contribution.
  • Organizational impact: Experience creating prototypes and/or reusable tools that help other designers and engineers improve their craft and work more effectively. Demonstrate how these capabilities were adopted and what changed in the quality or effectiveness of others’ work.
  • Collective direction and influence: Ability to align partners around a technical and experience direction, navigate disagreement, and lead ambiguous work across teams without relying on reporting authority.
  • AI and agent-assisted practice: Hands-on experience with AI-assisted coding and prototyping. Ability to provide useful context, evaluate generated code, test interactions, and choose tools based on quality and outcomes.

What You'll Be Doing & Why It Matters

Salesforce is hiring a Senior Director to lead Corporate Strategic Investments. The program invests in companies at every stage where the primary reason to invest is strategic: an equity position that tightens alignment between Salesforce and the company while driving outcomes that matter to Salesforce's customers, products, and partners.

This is a program at scale from day one. This leader will manage an existing portfolio on behalf of Salesforce and execute a significant volume of investments each year.

Investment opportunities are typically sourced through Salesforce product, go-to-market, and executive leaders who have identified a company of strategic importance through a customer relationship, a partnership, or product roadmap priorities. The Head of Corporate Strategic Investments is the person who turns that executive interest into a disciplined investment decision. This person will diligence the company, test the strategic rationale, structure the investment, and make sure the strategic value is actually realized after close.

This is a new role that reports to John Somorjai and is a stand-alone function with its own mandate and investment decisions. It is separate from Salesforce Ventures (SFV) and the Salesforce M&A deal team, but the teams will coordinate to route opportunities to the appropriate group.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Own the strategic investment pipeline. Be the primary point of contact for Salesforce product, go-to-market, partnerships, and executive leaders bringing forward companies of strategic importance. Triage quickly, prioritize ruthlessly, and give clear yes / no / not-yet answers.
  • Lead diligence end to end. Evaluate business quality, financial performance, market position, technology, and team. In parallel, rigorously test the strategic case: what Salesforce gets, who internally owns delivering it, and how it will be measured.
  • Pressure-test strategic rationale. Apply and help evolve the criteria for a strategic investment, which require strong Salesforce executive sponsorship plus one or more of the following: an existing or potential partnership, a product built on or leveraging Salesforce infrastructure, or a sector or technology outside SFV's investment focus.
  • Structure and execute transactions. Negotiate terms and coordinate any commercial, partnership, or go-to-market agreements that sit alongside the equity. Partner with Legal, Finance, Treasury, and Tax through close.
  • Drive approvals. Prepare clear, concise investment recommendations and approval materials for John Somorjai, Salesforce executive leadership, and the CEO / Chief Operating and Financial Officer (COFO) approval process.
  • Deliver strategic outcomes after close. Make sure the alignment that justified each investment actually happens: partnership milestones, product integration, joint go-to-market, and customer outcomes. Hold internal sponsors accountable and report on progress.
  • Manage the portfolio. Oversee the existing multi-billion-dollar corporate strategic portfolio, including performance, follow-on decisions, valuation, and liquidity. Where relevant, serve as Salesforce's board observer or representative.
  • Coordinate with SFV and Corporate Development. Coordinate with leaders to route each opportunity to the appropriate team.
  • Build the function. Set the operating cadence, investment framework, reporting, and success metrics for the program.



Minimum Requirements

  • 10+ years of corporate development or strategic investing experience at a large technology company, or comparable experience in growth equity, corporate venture, or investment banking.
  • Track record of leading private investments across stages through close, including structuring, negotiation, and approval. Experience deploying significant capital, including large-check investments, is a plus.
  • Experience pairing equity investments with commercial partnerships or other strategic agreements.
  • Deep understanding of enterprise software, AI, and cloud markets, and a strong working knowledge of how large platform companies partner, build, and buy.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication. Can distill a complex deal into a crisp recommendation for executive leadership.
  • Strong financial and valuation skills, business judgment, and attention to detail.
  • Comfortable building a new function with ambiguous scope inside a large, matrixed organization, and working effectively across Legal, Finance, Treasury, Product, and Sales.
  • Utmost respect for confidentiality; experience handling material non-public information (MNPI).
  • Undergraduate degree required; MBA or equivalent is a plus.

The Senior Builder Experience

  • Technical Ownership: Partner with a Deployment Strategist to own customer outcomes end-to-end. You're the senior technical authority in the room, ensuring deliverables meet the  highest engineering  standards, whether it was generated by an AI tool by a colleague or written by you directly. 
  • AI-Supported  Engineering: Cursor, Claude, and Salesforce coding products like Vibes are embedded in your  daily workflow. The conventions and patterns you develop tend to propagate through the team because other Builders look to your work as reference.
  • Roadmap Influence: Your field experience routes directly to Product and Engineering. The gaps you hit and the edge cases you encounter in real life customer environments become the features they ship. Senior Forward Deployed Engineers are the most credible voice in agentic AIproduct evolution.
  • Continuous Innovation: You're expected to stay at the forefront — piloting emerging AI tools, experimenting with new models and frameworks, and sharing what you learn with your team and customers.

What You'll Actually Be Building

  • Own end-to-end build and deployment of agentic AI solutions for Salesforce's most strategic customers — from architecture decisions through production handoff.
  • Design and ship agentic systems on the Agentforce platform: agent logic, tool calls, multi-agent orchestration, deterministic guardrails, and the integration patterns that hold up in enterprise environments. Your reference implementations become the basis for how other Builders approach similar problems.
  • Own the data lifecycle: model design, processing pipelines, and data readiness for AI applications across Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake, Databricks, and customer-specific platforms.
  • Resolve the technical blockers that other engineers can't — data integration failures, model deployment issues, orchestration breakdowns, performance regressions. These problems are routed to you because of your track record of solving them.
  • Build and maintain agent performance dashboards and customer KPI reporting to track deployment health and business outcomes across engagements.
  • Develop proofs-of-concept and MVPs quickly, with the judgment to know which decisions can be deferred and which need to be right the first time.

  • Mentor other Engineers through code reviews, pair sessions, and shared work. Most of your influence on developing engineers happens inside the same codebases you're building in.
  • Provide technical depth on at-risk or strategically critical deployments when senior engineering judgment is needed.
  • Surface field insights directly to Product and Engineering. The gaps and edge cases you encounter in real customer environments are some of the most valuable inputs to the Agentforce roadmap.
  • Partner with the Deployment Strategist on your team to translate complex customer business challenges into agentic solutions that actually ship.

  • You're an expert in at least one of Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or Apex, and conversant in the others.

What You'll Be Doing & Why It Matters

We're hiring systems and database engineers across experience levels to build Database.com and advance Hyper, Salesforce's database engine for interactive query processing.

Hyper powers analytics in Tableau and query processing in Salesforce Data 360. With Database.com, we're building on that foundation to give developers and AI agents direct access to a database for application data, transactions, analytics, and retrieval across cloud and local environments.

Depending on your interests and experience, you'll contribute to areas such as:

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Query optimization, query compilation, code generation, and parallel execution.
  • Storage engines, indexing, caching, compression, and efficient I/O.
  • Transactions, concurrency control, recovery, and concurrent read/write workloads.
  • Streaming ingestion, lakehouse writes, compaction, and open formats such as Apache Iceberg and Parquet as well as internal optimized storage formats.
  • Distributed systems, federated query processing, and serverless scheduling and resource isolation.
  • Local and embedded database execution, including WebAssembly.
  • Define the long-term architecture and technical strategy for Database.com and Hyper, align multiple teams around it, and act as the technical authority on the hardest design decisions.



Minimum Requirements

  • 15+ years of experience building systems software or database technology, with a track record of architecting large-scale systems and influencing technical strategy across organizations.

title: Deployment Strategist
descriptionHtml:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

About the Role

Customer impact from day one. Strategic clarity and Execution that sticks.


Salesforce is hiring Deployment Strategists — Strategic Builders who are customer-facing advisors, who define AI strategy, shape agentic solutions, and drive measurable adoption for enterprise customers. You'll work as part of a delivery team alongside Forward Deployed Engineers, translating complex business challenges into agentic AI deployments that go live and generate real value. Engagements are focused and time-bound — typically 12 weeks or less — and may span a single strategic account or multiple customers simultaneously. Your impact isn't just getting to deployment. It ensures customers realise lasting, scalable value from the solutions your team builds.


Key Responsibilities

  • Full Lifecycle Ownership: Lead end-to-end customer engagement across the complete value lifecycle — Identify → Commit → Deploy → Consume — owning outcomes at every stage, not just discovery or deal closure
  • AI Strategy & Architecture: Define the customer's Agentic AI strategy and roadmap. Lead design workshops, agent design sessions, and jobs-to-be-done analysis. Architect solutions spanning Salesforce's agentic AI platform, Data Cloud, and enterprise systems, with responsible AI governance baked in from the start.
  • Deployment Oversight & Program Management: Manage engagement delivery end-to-end timelines, stakeholder communication, risk escalation, and progress reporting. You are the operational backbone of your delivery team, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks.
  • Adoption & Consumption: Own adoption, consumption, and expansion metrics within your engagement scope. Identify blockers early and develop strategies to drive measurable value realization
  • Delivery Team Coordination: Partner closely with the Forward Deployed Engineers on your team to align strategy with technical execution. Keep the team focused, unblocked, and on track to hit delivery milestones.
  • AI-Supported Development: You'll be developing real customer solutions supported by leading-edge AI tools: Including 
  • Cursor, Claude, and our coding products like Vibes, to accelerate development.  
  • Customer Stakeholder Management: Serve as the primary customer-facing contact, building trust-based relationships with senior stakeholders and present proposals, decisions and outcomes in terms of business value, not just technical detail. 
  • AI Readiness: Assess customer readiness for AI adoption and guide change management and process transformation to maximise the benefits of intelligent agents
  • Product Feedback Loop: Synthesise field insights and translate them into actionable product feedback that influences Salesforce's Agentic AI platform roadmap.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years experience in strategic solutioning, technical advisory, or delivery leadership or programme management for enterprise cloud or SaaS technology
  • You have a degree in Computer Science or a related field
  • Prior customer-facing delivery experience (consulting, professional services, or technical advisory) - this is a requirement, not a nice-to-have
  • Demonstrated understanding of the Salesforce platform and ecosystem, including Agentic AI capabilities and Data Cloud
  • Working knowledge of one or more programming languages: Python, JavaScript, Java, or Apex
  • Proven ability to lead and own complex, ambiguous engagements end-to-end — from discovery through to measurable outcomes
  • Experience leading AI/LLM solution design, including agentic AI strategy, conversation design, and responsible AI practices
  • Strong project and programme management skills — ability to run multiple workstreams, manage stakeholder expectations, and keep delivery on track in ambiguous environments
  • Ability to travel 25% of the time to customer sites

Preferred Experience

  • Experience with Salesforce Data Cloud, Agentforce platform, and Salesforce CRM (Sales, Service, Marketing)
  • Experience designing and deploying AI solutions in regulated industries (e.g., public sector, financial services, healthcare)
  • Salesforce platform certifications (e.g., Data Cloud Consultant, Agentforce Specialist, Application Architect) or similar platform certifications such as Microsoft, Oracle, or similar platforms.
  • Background in change management, organisational design, or enterprise transformation
  • Experience with AI/ML concepts beyond LLMs, including NLP, RAG architectures, and model evaluation frameworks
  • A get-things-done mindset with strong bias for action — comfortable operating in unstructured fast moving environments 

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

Accommodations

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form.

Please note that Salesforce uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help our recruiters assess and evaluate candidates’ resumes and qualifications throughout the recruiting process. Humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. Please see our Candidate Privacy Statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of AI tools and opt out options.

It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey.
